proposals.relationship: Hill questions Yates’s explanation of Hermeticism’s displacement by mechanical philosophy and argues for greater weight on political fear of radicalism.
proposals.evidence_note: Own complete 1973 review calls the supersession account less convincing, questions the explanatory weight of the 1659 Dee diary publication, and stresses social and political hostility to Rosicrucian radicalism. He also suggests her dynastic starting point may understate its radical associations. This is a scoped explanatory disagreement, partly developing hints he expressly credits Yates herself with supplying, alongside strong praise for her discoveries and future research possibilities. It does not reject her whole work or claim her original book has been newly read. The existing reverse Yates-to-Hill resource edge 506 remains exact.
